AND THE SIGN IS NEGATIVE, WHICH SAYS MORE THAN A ZERO WOULD. Applying the
dilution correction makes the prediction WORSE. Two readings, both allowed:
(a) Larsson's normalisation already absorbed dilution, so lambda_L = d + mu is
the correct reading and I-B is the right arm -- in which case M* = alpha
Theta and the ODE is exactly an identity map on its input;
(b) the per-gene half-life is noisy enough that multiplying by any function of
it degrades a good predictor. Spearman(mRNA half-life, mRNA copies) is
reported below at the leakage disclosure so this can be weighed.
This loop cannot separate (a) from (b) and does not pretend to.
THE HONEST READING, PREDECLARED AS THE EXPECTED OUTCOME: at the mRNA tier this
two-tier ODE is a UNITS CONVERSION of somebody else's abundance measurement. The
integrator is correct (I1), it converges (I7), and it adds nothing the input did
not already contain. Theta is Larsson's fitted mean expression by construction --
I3 measured that -- so Arm I tests whether one lab's mean scRNA-seq level predicts
another lab's mRNA copy number. That is a real and non-circular test. It is not a
simulation of transcription.

DOES THE SECOND HOP ADD ANYTHING? -- the I5 question again, one tier up:
M* alone against prot_copies            rho +0.4590
P* = k_sp M*/b against prot_copies      rho +0.5593   gain +0.1003
unlike the mRNA tier, dividing by the protein loss rate is a MEASURED per-gene
quantity that the input did not contain, so a gain here is the ODE doing work.
TIER-TO-TIER CHANGE: mRNA rho +0.4649 -> protein rho +0.5593 (+0.0944); 2x accuracy 55.9% -> 29.6%. Rank
agreement rises while fold accuracy falls -- protein copy numbers span
six orders of magnitude and are easier to RANK and harder to HIT than mRNA copies.
the second hop adds a measured protein half-life and one constant, and that is the
entire model of translation here -- no codon usage, no ribosome competition, no
regulation. Loop 92 already showed ribosomes run at 22.3% utilisation, so a
capacity-blind constant is not obviously wrong; it is just not informative.

a PERFECTLY STABLE protein still needs 104 h to reach 95%, because

WITHIN A CELL CYCLE. A model that reports steady-state protein levels -- this one
included, and every FBA and every proteome-constraint model in this repository --
is reporting a limit the cell spends its life approaching and never reaching.
LEAKAGE DISCLOSURE -- the one place Arm I touches Schwanhausser other than as truth
Arm I-A's correction d/(d+mu) is built from the Schwanhausser mRNA HALF-LIFE. If
half-life were strongly related to copy number, part of the answer would leak in.
Spearman(mRNA half-life, mRNA copies) = +0.3411 over 4,190 genes.
Half-lives are not abundances and are measured in a separate experiment, but the
number is reported so the reader can price the concern instead of trusting it away.
